observedImprovements: The new authored open arch and heavy stone shoulders are visually present in actual original 66.10–66.70s gameplay instead of invisible in a separate DCC viewport, at the correctly proven R35B Road6 site.
Real opening/negative space can be read in 66.25–66.55; original road centre lanes, stage obstacle warning and HUD remain legible in reviewed frames.
R36 has replaced the three orange diagnostic boxes with an actual editable studio DCC structure, but this does not imply ART acceptance.
failures: The dominant visual is still a large, smooth gray angular arch/bridge with attached geometric chunks. It reads as another isolated generic ring, not one original commercially credible integrated tidal lock.

The 39.9m simulated visual head drop is not clearly visible as working water; the road-facing left sea remains predominantly a flat cyan band, so the intended source 19–gate–plunge basin hydraulic connection is visually unproven.

The exposed stone landing, mechanical gate, copper pulley and spillway geometry mostly compress into a flat icon/silhouette; their load path and water operation are not readable during a ~0.5s fly-by.
No convincing coherent industrial architecture beyond one isolated water gate; no high material/detail quality and no artistic spatial depth comparable to the project's quality bar.
R36 confirms source placement but not human enjoyment, fairness, or predictable high-speed hazard readability as human-tested claims.
